subject: Re: ACME  Reranking model fit & A/B plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: rerank evals

Alex  thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the immediate next steps we agreed on:

- Goal: improve search relevancy on product pages using a reranking model; primary KPIs are NDCG@10 and MRR (search-to-click relevance).
- Constraints: 100ms token-latency SLO for candidate reranker in the product path; privacy: no customer PII leaves Acme systems.
- Data: you said you can share a 20k prompt set (anonymized) and click-through labels for a 30-day window.

Action items we covered:
1) You share the anonymized prompt set + label sample (Priya / data team).
2) Redwood runs a rerank model fit/eval across candidate models (baseline & 2 alternatives) and returns NDCG/MRR, per-query breakdowns, and a suggested A/B rollout plan.
3) We'll highlight any quality regressions vs baseline and propose mitigations (prompting changes, candidate thresholds, or fallback).

I've attached the prompt set format + an example (acme_promptset_v3.jsonl) and will begin the first-pass eval once we get your sample. Expect preliminary NDCG/MRR numbers in 24-48 hours after data arrives.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

References: link to shared folder with eval templates and dashboard: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBc...acme-rerank-evals

Thanks Marissa - this looks right. Quick questions before we send the sample:

- For the evals, which exact model checkpoints and quantization levels will you run? We want to understand compute and latency tradeoffs.
- Do you need any specific tokenization or normalization applied to our labels?
- On the A/B plan: would you recommend starting with a partial rollout (e.g., 5-10%) and a short ramp? Curious how you normally instrument for regressions.

I'll coordinate with Priya to get the anonymized 20k sample today or tomorrow.

-Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-26T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: ACME rerank evals: first-pass results + notes

Alex / Priya - attached are the first-pass artifacts: acme_rerank_results_20260625.csv and ndcg_mrr_plot.png. Summary of what we ran and key takeaways:

What we evaluated:
- Baseline: your current production scorer (lightweight heuristic), treated as control.
- Model A: cross-encoder reranker (bert-large-ish architecture, FP16) - higher latency, high quality.
- Model B: distilled cross-encoder (quantized int8) - lower latency, slightly lower quality.

Metrics (aggregated):
- Baseline NDCG@10: 0.432
- Model A NDCG@10: 0.512 (+8.0% relative uplift)
- Model B NDCG@10: 0.487 (+5.3% relative uplift)

- Baseline MRR: 0.301
- Model A MRR: 0.359 (+19.3% relative uplift)
- Model B MRR: 0.342 (+13.6% relative uplift)

Per-segment notes: Model A shows strong gains on long-tail queries (low impression volume) but has a measurable latency cost (p50 increase ~45ms vs baseline in our test harness). Model B provides most of the quality gain at ~20ms p50 overhead - better for tighter SLOs.

Quality regression concerns we flagged:
- For ~2.4% of queries, Model A re-ranked results that previously matched exact SKU matches lower (edge-case for exact-match intent). We've attached a small sample (rows flagged in the CSV) showing the mismatch.
- These regressions are concentrated in a specific query prefix set (searches starting with "sku:") - recommend a simple prefix rule to short-circuit reranker for exact-match SKU queries.

Artifacts & reproducibility:
- acme_promptset_v3.jsonl (format you provided) - used for eval sampling.
- acme_rerank_results_20260625.csv - includes per-query NDCG, MRR, and top-k result diffs.
- ndcg_mrr_plot.png - aggregate plots.

Next recommended steps (short term):
1) Implement prefix short-circuit for SKU queries (fallback to baseline).
2) Start A/B test with Model B at 10% traffic for 2 weeks + monitoring (NDCG, MRR, page engagement, rollback guard).
3) If Model B is stable, roll to 25% and evaluate. Consider Model A for high-value buckets where latency budget is higher or as a staged treatment.

I'll loop in David and Aditya for an A/B plan and monitoring dashboard. If you'd like, we can also run an additional eval with a constrained-latency Model A variant (smaller width or earlier stopping) to see if we can recover the SKU regressions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_rerank_results_20260625.csv; ndcg_mrr_plot.png
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-27T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed A/B plan and safety guardrails

Alex - following up with an A/B rollout proposal and monitoring/rollback plan. TL;DR: start with Model B at 10% for 14 days, evaluate both metric-level and business-level signals, automatic rollback if regression exceeds thresholds. Details:

Experiment setup:
- Variant: Model B (quantized int8 reranker). Control: Baseline scorer.
- Allocation: 10% variant, 90% control. Randomized at session level to avoid user-level oscillation.
- Duration: minimum 14 days, target 28 days for seasonality coverage.

Metrics & thresholds (automatic rollback triggers):
- Primary: NDCG@10 delta <= -0.01 absolute vs control (i.e., if NDCG drops by more than 0.01).
- Secondary: MRR delta <= -0.02 absolute; click-through rate (CTR) decrease > 1.5% absolute.
- Business guardrails: bounce rate increase > 2% absolute for product pages.

Monitoring plan:
- Near real-time: per-minute sampling of a 1% traffic probe with aggregated p50/p95 latencies and top-level NDCG/MRR.
- Daily: full-sample NDCG/MRR calculation and per-query diagnostic joins for regressions. CSVs pushed to shared Drive folder and a basic dashboard (link above).

Mitigations for identified regressions:
1) Fast fallback route: if query matches SKU prefix, route to baseline.
2) Canary prompt tuning: for queries showing degraded rank, apply a two-pass approach: candidate filter + tuned prompt for reranker.
3) Rollback: immediate 100% rollback to baseline and notify stakeholders if any automatic trigger fires.

If you confirm this plan, we can schedule the 10% rollout for next Tuesday (2026-06-30) and provide daily readouts.

- David Kim
Product Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Proposed A/B plan and safety guardrails

Thanks - this looks good and conservative, which we appreciate. Confirming:

- We'll implement the SKU prefix short-circuit on our side (Priya's team will push the rule by EOD Monday).
- Please proceed with the Model B 10% test starting 2026-06-30. We'll watch the shared dashboard and expect daily updates.

One ask: can you include a short per-query sample in the daily digest showing top 5 result changes for any query where NDCG delta <= -0.02? That will help our search QA triage.

Appreciate the quick turnaround - excited to see the impact.

- Alex
Head of Search, Acme Corp
